Second-reading addendum, p. 179, theorem 3.9.1: the inherited cross-cover repair is retained, with its ledger wording expanded to the whole clause. An independent counterexample to the printed self-trace version was checked. Let X=S^1×S^1 and let F be the integral rank-one local system with monodromy −1 on both circle generators. Its cellular cochains have d0(a)=(−2a,−2a) and d1(b,c)=2b−2c, so H^1(X,F)=Z/2. Take a good three-arc covering of each circle, horizontal annular strips Rh and vertical strips Rv. Let S consist of X, the empty set and finite intersections within either strip covering, and let R(X)={Rh,Rv}. On every proper nonempty A in S take only the trace of its own strip covering; it contains A itself, hence has zero positive Čech cohomology, and its self-traces satisfy the printed conditions. On X all section groups in either strip Čech complex vanish, because the local system has monodromy −1 along each annulus. Thus A(1) holds and B(0) is vacuous. The common refinement Rh∩Rv consists of contractible rectangles, on each of which the nonzero H^1 class vanishes. The printed conclusion for n=1 is false. The corrected cross-cover condition excludes this example. This is a mathematical check by the primary reviewer; no external edition was consulted.
